source_title: 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards: ‘General Hospital’ Wins Best Daytime Drama
source_excerpt:
The 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards were presented Friday night, with General Hospital taking home the top prize of best daytime drama.
The series, which went into Friday night’s show up for 13 awards, won three other awards and saw its Genie Francis receive the lifetime achievement award. Beyond the Gates also won four awards, with star Tamara Tunie winning best actress in a daytime drama series. Best actor in a daytime drama went to The Bold and the Beautiful ‘s Scott Clifton.
Tunie, who won her first Daytime Emmy, paid tribute to the “host of Black actresses who paved the way for me, and I feel them as I stand here tonight, beginning with the legendary Cicely Tyson, the first Black woman to appear on a daytime television show, The Guiding Light .” Related Stories TV The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards
The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award
Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards
Fellow best actress nominee Heather Tom, from The Bold and the Beautiful , was eyeing a record-setting seventh trophy, which would have made her the most awarded actress in daytime history.
The Young and the Restless led this year’s nominees with 18 nominations. Though it only won three awards, two of those came in the supporting performer categories. Roger Howarth was named best supporting actor, and Beth Maitland was named best supporting actress.
The Kelly Clarkson Show won five awards, including best daytime talk series, but the singer-host of the now-completed talk show didn’t appear to be at the Daytime Emmys . And Clarkson didn’t win the award for best daytime talk series host. Instead that honor went to fellow former talk show host Sherri Shepherd, whose eponymous talk show was canceled after four seasons.
Other notable winners include Tracee Ellis Ross, who won best travel and adventure program for her Solo Traveling show; Keke Palmer, who won for her work executive producing Glam Through the Ages ; and Ina Garten, who won best culinary host for her Be My Guest Food Network series, which was named best culinary instructional series.
Midway through the ceremony, NATAS chair Terry O’Reilly offered a timely, political speech, just days ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Speaking about a congressman who was jailed in 1798 after criticizing the president in print, O’Reilly highlighed the power of the people.
“The free press in 1800 was not saved by a court. It was saved by citizens who were engaged and informed,” he said.
Turning to the present day, O’Reilly called out “the most sustained effort to control what Americans see and hear in this country that were faced in my lifetime.” He cited specifically journalists being banned from covering the Pentagon and president, the DOJ antitrust investigation into the White House TV press pool and the challenge to the news exemption enjoyed by late night and daytime programs, including The View .
“It is not much of a leap, from silencing political speech, to suppressing creative expression,” O’Reilly added. “The characters, the storylines, the points of view that someone in power decides are no longer welcome. Here, in the cradle of Hollywood, this town of all towns, we know where that can lead. We have seen what happens when those in power begin drawing up lists of people and pops and ideas that they are willing to label as un-American. We should never wish to see that again.”
Turning to the “consequential” midterms on Tuesday, O’Reilly issued a call to those in the audience: “Let’s stand together to resist those who would seek comfort in a quieter media.”
And NATAS additionally inducted a number of individuals into its Gold and Silver Circle Society, recognizing industry leaders who’ve demonstrated enduring contributions to television through their 50 or 25 years in industry. The 2026 Gold Circle inductees are Allen Media Group CEO Byron Allen, performer Patrika Darbo, actor-director-producer Francesca James and host-producer Meredith Vieira. The Silver Circle inductees are Fox TV Stations executive vp, programming and development Stephen Brown and announcer warm-up host Rubin Ervin.
The Hollywood Reporter won its first Daytime Emmy , taking home the award for best arts and popular culture program for THR ’s Off Script roundtable series.
Fellow PMC brand IndieWire additionally won best editing for a daytime studio program for its craft roundtables, with Trevor Wallace accepting for the brand.
The 53rd Daytime Emmy Awards ceremony took place on Friday, Oct. 30 at the Hollywood Palladium.
